text:
pete: Hi all, new hire question — following the repo quickstart but my service (running on host) can't talk to Postgres in docker-compose. App shows `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432`.

pete: `docker ps` shows the postgres container healthy and `docker logs` says ready. I'm confused why localhost refuses.

emma: welcome! did your compose map the container port to the host? share the pg service snippet.

pete: snippet from repo:```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    volumes:
      - ./data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432"
```

ryan: ah that `- "5432"` bit is subtle. It publishes the port in some setups but doesn't guarantee a host bind like `"5432:5432"` does. If your app runs on the host you need host->container mapping or use host.docker.internal.

pete: changed to `"5432:5432"` and recreated containers. `docker ps` now shows `0.0.0.0:5432->5432/tcp` but host psql still says connection refused.

emma: two quick checks: 1) do you have a system Postgres already bound to 5432? `lsof -i:5432` will tell. 2) any permission errors in logs from the bind mount? sometimes container can't start DB fully because of host FS perms.

pete: `lsof` shows nothing. `docker logs` earlier had `could not open lock file "postmaster.pid": Permission denied` but after `chown` to 999 it later printed ready.

ryan: are you on WSL2 by chance? Networking quirks there can make localhost behave differently.

pete: yes WSL2 Ubuntu.

emma: in WSL2 it's common to run into host/VM network boundaries. Two good options: 1) run your app inside a dev container so it can resolve service names like `postgres` directly, or 2) use `host.docker.internal` from the host, but on WSL you may need to add `extra_hosts: - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"` to compose.

pete: I tried `host.docker.internal` but it wouldn't resolve until I added `extra_hosts`. After that `psql -h host.docker.internal -p 5432 -U postgres` still refused though.

ryan: check that the postgres container actually has the port published (we saw it does). On WSL sometimes Docker binds to the VM address not the WSL localhost. Try `docker inspect postgres` and look at NetworkSettings->Ports to see where it's mapped. Also try connecting from inside a small alpine container on the same compose network: `docker run --rm --network <proj>_default appropriate/curl nc -vz postgres 5432` to verify container-to-container reachability.

pete: running an alpine test container on the compose network connects to host `postgres:5432` fine. So DNS and container networking works. The issue is host->container path.

emma: that matches WSL strangeness. If you need host-based fast reloads, easiest workaround: map container port to a different host port like `"5433:5432"` and connect to localhost:5433, or run the dev server in a container.

pete: mapped to 5433, restarted, and now psql to localhost:5433 connects! That works. Thanks.

ryan: FYI, for Postgres data we prefer named volumes in dev to avoid host FS permission problems: `volumes:
  - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` + top-level `volumes:
  pgdata:`. If you need a host mount for inspection, do an init step to chown the folder to 999:999.

pete: switching to named volume fixed the earlier permission error too.

infra-bot: (infra) postgres:14 started and listening :white_check_mark:

emma: TL;DR for new-hires: 1) service hostnames (postgres, redis) only resolve between containers; 2) if app runs on host you must map host ports explicitly (`"host:container"`) or use host.docker.internal (WSL may need extra_hosts); 3) named volumes avoid permission headaches on bind mounts; 4) run app in a dev container for the cleanest local parity.

pete: awesome, grateful for the help. I'll open a tiny README PR noting the WSL binding gotchas and port mapping tips. :tada:
